synonyms: Croton capitatus var. lindheimeri (Engelm. & A.Gray) Müll.Arg.
taxonomic_note: Accepted as a distinct species by current POWO and Flora of North America. Older Central Texas material commonly appears under Croton capitatus var. lindheimeri.
look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST — LINDHEIMER'S DOVEWEED / WOOLLY CROTON: a robust MONOECIOUS annual with young yellow-brown (ochraceous) woolly hairs, predominantly ACUTE leaf tips and some rounded or heart-shaped leaf bases. The key distinction from true C. capitatus is in FEMALE flowers: 7–8 long woolly sepals (about 5–7 mm) with tips STRAIGHT or only slightly INCURVED, NOT flaring strongly outward after flowering. Three styles branch twice, often 12 terminal branches. The source-licensed existing habit and flowering photos cannot confirm actual mature sepal posture; keep this image gap. Do not confuse C. lindheimeri with C. lindheimerianus, the much smaller low annual with short female sepals and only SIX style ends.

morphology_keys.comparison_training: Separate from true C. capitatus with young pubescence color, consistently acute leaves, and non-recurving pistillate sepals.

comparisons.key_distinctions: C. lindheimeri tends toward ochraceous young growth, acute leaf tips, female sepals 5–7 mm whose tips stay straight to slightly incurved, with styles divided TWICE (often 12 ends). Strict C. capitatus often has SOME blunt/mucronate leaves and female sepals 7–10 mm that flare outward/recurve at or after anthesis. In contrast C. lindheimerianus is a smaller low-branched annual with 3 mm pistillate sepals and styles only once-forked (six ends). Similar color/fuzz alone does not identify any species.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.title: Woolly croton: Lindheimer's without outward-flaring female sepals

steps.look: Robust annual with a main shoot and hairy branches, not persistently woody
steps.what: Do not mistake its tall annual habit for shrub C. fruticulosus.
Supports a tentative Lindheimer's ID; hue alone does not split it from C. capitatus.

steps.look: Mostly sharply acute leaf tips, variable rounded to heart-shaped bases
steps.what: Compare several mature and upper leaves rather than one. Not every leaf is diagnostic.

steps.look: 5–7 mm persistent woolly sepals, mostly straight or slightly turned inward
steps.what: Take side view at anthesis and fruit. True C. capitatus typically shows long sepals flaring outward or recurved.

steps.look: Female styles branch twice to around twelve ultimate tips
steps.what: Only true exposed pistillate flowers allow this. Existing photo views do not count the tips.

photo_diagnostic_lesson.memory_rule: LINDHEIMER'S: acute leaves + ochraceous young wool + female sepal tips that DON'T FLARE OUT.

field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Croton lindheimeri: actual female sepal posture determines the split
steps: Observe a robust woolly annual with acute foliage.
Check young shoot hairs: often ochraceous rather than clean-white, but not decisive.
Find pistillate flowers and compare sepal tips at anthesis and mature fruit: STRAIGHT/SLIGHTLY INWARD.
Photograph clear leaf apices and bases with a scale; compare strict C. capitatus.
Do not count old C. capitatus var. lindheimeri reports as true C. capitatus.
field_photo_quickcheck.field_rule: Ochraceous young wool + predominantly acute leaves + female sepals NOT outward-recurved supports C. lindheimeri.
field_photo_quickcheck.warning: Current images do not independently prove sepal orientation or ultimate style-tip counts. Preserve county native-range hold.
